turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, parking was a whole thing. Um, we came in cause his skin's yellow.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ten days old?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, ten days yesterday.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did you notice the yellow?
[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Err, umm, day four, maybe day five. I can't really pin the day down.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Wah.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breast or formula?
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Both. Breast milk, and we give some formula after. He feeds about every four hours.
[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My sister keeps texting that four hours is too long. He just knocks out though.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any cough?
[SEG0013] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He grunts when he's on the breast. I wouldn't call it a cough. Maybe a tiny bit. I don't know.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Vomiting or diarrhea?
[SEG0015] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting. And the poop is that yellow seedy stuff, not diarrhea. He does spit up a little after the bottle.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Mmm. Wah.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight from the nurse is seven pounds 1 ounce.
[SEG0018] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was seven pounds six ounces when he was born, so he's down a bit.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Skin is yellow from the face onto the chest. Sclera are yellow. Belly is soft, no masses.
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been so fussy, doctor. Barely naps, and I am wiped. We had the baseball game on at two a.m., don't ask.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): This is newborn jaundice. Could be ordinary physiologic jaundice or breast milk jaundice. I'm not locking that in.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll draw a bilirubin today.
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): In the hospital they said the bilirubin was borderline. They didn't give me a number.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Discharge sheet?
[SEG0025] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's on the counter at home. Of course.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medicines?
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You mean me, I'm the one nursing. Amlowdipine, uh, ten milligrams, no, five milligrams, for the pressure, every morning.
[SEG0028] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The cholesterol one at night. It's atorva-something, forty, wait, 20 milligrams. Sugar tablets too, metforman, five hundred twice a day.
[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, the one from the shop. I stopped the iron in March, killed my stomach.
[SEG0030] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A friend said gripe water. We never gave it to him.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't start that. Keep breast and formula, and wake him if he goes past four hours.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Uh.
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I read the yellow can hurt their brain. Is that what's happening?
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's what the level is for. I'm not saying that from a look.
[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Wet diapers?
[SEG0037] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah. Plenty, pretty much every feed.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Be back tomorrow morning and we'll go through the result.
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he looks worse tonight?
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the yellow spreads to his legs or he stops feeding, come in sooner.
[SEG0041] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Drop the formula?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): No. Keep both. Just feed him.
[SEG0043] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Neighbor's kid got some light-up blanket. We doing that?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not booking phototherapy right now. Depends on today's number.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): Mmph.
[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's rooting again. Figures, right in the office.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lab will draw him before you go. Tomorrow morning, this clinic.
[SEG0048] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. Thanks.

spec.situation: Parents with a ten-day-old baby, yellow skin and feeding every four hours; weight read by the nurse; breast milk plus formula; blood test for bilirubin planned today.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

omissions.text: Patient age was stated as 10 days old (ten days yesterday).
Birth weight was 7 lb 6 oz, compared with current weight 7 lb 1 oz (down a bit from birth).
Feeding interval of every 4 hours was noted as potentially too long by family; doctor specifically advised waking him if he goes past 4 hours.

Negative finding asked and answered: no cough was not clearly established; family said he grunts on the breast and 'wouldn't call it a cough,' 'maybe a tiny bit,' indicating uncertainty rather than a definite negative.
Stools were described as yellow and seedy.
Wet diapers were reported as plentiful, pretty much every feed.
Prior hospital bilirubin was reported as 'borderline' but with no number available.
Doctor said newborn jaundice could be ordinary physiologic jaundice or breast milk jaundice, and explicitly was 'not locking that in' (diagnosis not confirmed).
Lab draw was to be done before leaving today.
Phototherapy was discussed and specifically not being booked right now; decision depends on today's bilirubin result.
